explanations.explanation: Shinar it is, friend. The people journey eastward, find a plain in the land of Shinar and settle there (Genesis 11:2). Put that name in your back pocket, because this plain is where the whole story happens. Good start, baker.

Goshen is a place you'll meet later in Genesis, where Israel settles in Egypt (Genesis 47:27). This crowd lands somewhere else. They find a plain in the land of Shinar and settle there (Genesis 11:2). Mixing up two place names is easy. I do it with the drawer where I keep my spatula.

Moab is a fair guess, but this passage puts the people somewhere else. Journeying eastward, they find a plain in the land of Shinar and settle there (Genesis 11:2). Shinar is the name to hold onto. That's where the bricks start stacking up.

Stone is right, baker. The text says, “So they used brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.” (Genesis 11:3) Brick took the place of stone, and tar took the place of mortar. Swapping the whole building kit, that's some bold shopping.

Wood sounds sturdy, I'll give you that. But the text says, “So they used brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.” (Genesis 11:3) Wood never makes the list. These folks baked bricks and let them do the job of stone. I spent years in a junk drawer next to a twist tie, so believe me, I know a thing or two about building with whatever's lying around. Nobody ever built a tower out of a twist tie, though. We tried in my head.

Straw is a fair guess, since straw and bricks go together in your head. But this verse never mentions it. It says, “So they used brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.” (Genesis 11:3) Stone is the one the bricks replaced.

explanations.answer: To make a name for themselves
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. They say, “…that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.” (Genesis 11:4) They want the name, plain and simple. I think a name that big takes a lot of bricks.

explanations.answer: To guard the plain from enemies
explanations.explanation: Nice thinking, but no enemies show up in this passage. The people say the city and tower are so “…that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.” (Genesis 11:4) Guarding the plain never comes up. Their reason is about a name.

Keeping watch for another flood is a clever thought, and Genesis does tell of a flood earlier (Genesis 7:17). But this passage gives a different reason. The people say, “…that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.” (Genesis 11:4) Their reason is a name, and no flood watch is mentioned.

True, friend. In the same breath as making a name, they say they build so they will “…not be scattered over the face of all the earth.” (Genesis 11:4) Two goals, one tower. Keep that line in your pocket, because it comes back at the end.

Close, but it's true. The people say they build “…that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.” (Genesis 11:4) Not being scattered is right there in their plan. It's easy to read past with that tower stealing the spotlight.

explanations.answer: Nothing they plan will be out of their reach
explanations.explanation: Right on, baker. The LORD says, “…then nothing they devise will be beyond them.” (Genesis 11:6) One people, one language, and whatever they plan is within reach. That's a whole lot of teamwork, and the text says it plainly.

explanations.answer: Their city will grow too big for the plain
explanations.explanation: Room to grow is a creative guess, but the LORD never brings it up. He says, “…then nothing they devise will be beyond them.” (Genesis 11:6) His words are about whatever they devise, and the size of the plain doesn't come into it. Nobody in this passage is complaining about square footage.

explanations.answer: Their tower will fall before it is finished
explanations.explanation: A tower falling over before it's done would be a plot twist, but the LORD doesn't say that. He says, “If they have begun to do this as one people speaking the same language, then nothing they devise will be beyond them.” (Genesis 11:6) That's the whole “if” and the whole “then,” right there. I think it's like a group chat where everybody finally agrees on a time. Scary, that kind of teamwork.

That's it, friend. The LORD says, “Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.” (Genesis 11:7) The plan is about their speech. Bricks and tower stay out of it.

I see why you'd pick it, since the tower has been the talk of the whole passage. But the LORD says, “Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.” (Genesis 11:7) He doesn't say He'll bring the tower down. He goes after their speech. Picture it: one person says "pass the tar," and the person next to them hears something that sounds like "my cousin's a tuba." That's a whole different workday!

I can see why you'd say it, all those bricks sitting there. But the LORD's words are, “Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.” (Genesis 11:7) Not one brick gets broken in His plan. Language is the target.

Not quite, baker. The text says, “So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they stopped building the city.” (Genesis 11:8) The scattering came, and the building stopped. I think a crew that suddenly can't understand each other has a hard time saying "pass the tar." Picture getting a blank stare back!

False is right, friend. The text says, “So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they stopped building the city.” (Genesis 11:8) The building ended. I think a crew that can't understand each other has a hard time passing the tar.

Babel, baker, you've got it. The text says, “That is why it is called Babel, for there the LORD confused the language of the whole world…” (Genesis 11:9) The name comes from what happened there. It's a name that stuck.

Nineveh has a nice ring to it, but this verse names another place. It says, “That is why it is called Babel, for there the LORD confused the language of the whole world…” (Genesis 11:9) The verse even gives the reason for the name. Babel is the answer here, baker.

Erech does appear in Genesis 10:10, so it's a fair place to land. But this verse names a different spot. It says, “That is why it is called Babel, for there the LORD confused the language of the whole world…” (Genesis 11:9) Babel is the name for the place where the language got confused.
